txt: He douses you with the odd-smelling spray -- a double helping as you present your other arm pit -- and then gives you a satisfied nod.
He douses you with the odd-smelling spray and then gives you a satisfied nod.
He eyes you sceptically. "All right -- what cryptids, precisely? I usually discuss these things with *specialists*, so I don't know what..."
The ageing cryptozoologist breaks into a hideous coughing fit.
The cryptozoologist's face flushes with indignation. "Of course we have!"
There's a cylinder on the ground in which the man is arranging some netting. It looks like some kind of trap. He notices you.
"'A science person'?" He snarls. "The *so-called* science community hasn't accepted me as one of their own quite yet."
"'Ramblings'? Nonsense! Your description of the phasmid is the most precise I've ever heard!"
"*And*, I suspect it may also have developed other *specialized techniques* to protect itself from predators... or scientists, in our present case."
"*Autocannibalistic locusts*? I appreciate your *unconventional* thinking, officer, but really, cryptids aren't your area of expertise."
"*Completely* empty?" The cryptozoologist's eyes grow wide.
"*Formerly* the most dangerous, yes... But do you know the most dangerous *living* cryptid?"
"*Give up*? After we've come so far? Not a chance!"
"*Real*..." He scoffs at the concept. "I know you think one is a respectable profession while the other is superstition, everyone does!"
"...the way it moved, the colour, how some of its limbs were white like marble..." He breathes excitedly. "It matched *perfectly* with what I know from other accounts! It was amazing."
"A *different* cryptid?" The cryptozoologist furrows his heavy brow.
"A flightless *cursor owl* found in the Semenine isles. Its long legs permit the Nnong Okk to run faster than any other avian, perhaps any other *animal*, who knows?"
"A willow person. It's a long story, one non-specialists would find rather dull."
"AND LEAVE THE TRAPS? ABSOLUTELY NOT!" he yells in response. "I won't let Lena down..."
"Ack! Of course. Thank you for passing along the message. That damned water lock is broken, and we can't go all the way around the 8/81..."
"Ack, so that's what this is." He ignores your jab. "Lena sent you. Can't say I blame her -- we've been here for days. That damned water lock is broken, and we can't go under the 8/81..."

"Actually, no..." His tone changes. "Excuse me for getting emotional, this is a big deal for us. You've helped us *twice* now -- and brought some great news, too. My gratitude, *and* the gratitude of the Société Cryptozoologique de Revachol, is yours."
"After waiting in hiding for hours, I saw a figure slip from one of the trees, a lavender shadow dashing through the grove..."
"Agreed. Yet there is always a chance, albeit a small one, of a truly *good* surprise. One simply needs to look at the history of science -- serendipities abound!"
"All right." He remains guarded.
"Although -- probably because her life ended as a result of her work in Katla -- no one remembers her contributions to the search for the Nnong Okk."
"An *unconfirmed* sighting is just a story."
"And I'm eager to return to her, I assure you -- but I can't leave before we've finished with these traps."
"And it shouldn't. Nature does not concern herself with ethical propositions. As a scientist, my interest is *strictly dispassionate*."
"And that's not all! Some of the slaughterhouse apprentices went hiking by a nearby creek and saw a moose nibbling on an unidentified carcass!"
"Another one?" he seems angry for a second, but then settles down.
"Another we set in Land's End, to the northeast. It's behind a small sand dune there, on your way to the old radio tower. After the church."
"Anyway..." He settles down. "There is *more* than enough evidence to justify a thorough *search* for the dread moose. Let's close the subject, before it turns into an argument."
"Are you enjoying yourself, darling?"
"At least, that's the intention. The net isn't a perfect solution, but we didn't want to use anything that might damage the specimen's delicate exoskeleton."
"Believe me, you won't *guess* it. You either know, or you don't." He corrects his hat and says -- as if it's the most sensible thing in the world...
"Bring it to me at once. Just make sure the trap is closed tight."
"But I cannot describe how these defences work -- much less how they evolved -- without studying a live specimen."
"But that's not all! Some of the slaughterhouse apprentices went hiking by a nearby creek and saw a moose nibbling on an unidentified carcass!"
"By *wöman* you mean my wife, I assume. I will return to her -- but I can't leave before we've finished with these traps."
"By all means..." He coughs and wipes his mouth.
"By which I mean," he says, gathering himself, "I've heard enough first-hand accounts to believe quite firmly that the Insulindian phasmid is more than mere superstition."
"C'mon, Gary, it's never that black and white."
"Caught the bug, I see." He cracks an unwieldy smile. "It's easier to get caught up in the *search* than you'd imagine."
"Confirmed," he replies quickly. "It's 100% verified and meets all the standards of an authentic cryptid sighting."
"DON'T WORRY, GARY. I'LL HANDLE IT."
"Did he?" He lowers his voice. "That one's a hoax. Some Seraise rice farmers set fire to rhinoceros cadavers and used them scare tourists."
"Did you?" He seems incredulous. "It is almost as difficult to confirm a hoax as it is to confirm a sighting..." A cough.

"Do you know what the success rate in pharmacological research is? 0.000003% of bio-reactive agents have reproducibly beneficial effects. Yet science persists in the search for medicine. *As* we persist in our search for new species."
"Don't you remember that method I showed you back in... never mind."

"Even simply catching a glimpse of the Insulindian phasmid would be the apex of my -- of *any* -- cryptozoologist's career. But to study it and its defences, find out how it's stayed hidden so long..." He shakes his head.
"Everything from forgotten regional lore to newspaper accounts like the one that brought us here to look for the phasmid. I keep a very open mind."

"Furthermore," he raises his finger. "I am not saying it was a *confirmed* sighting. I am painfully aware of what goes into verifying such things. There is a serious possibility that I saw a squirrel, or a trick of the light. I am my own harshest critic."
"GARY! WHAT'S GOING ON?!"

"Gary and I painted an entire grove's worth of trees in slow-drying paint. It was a bright lavender colour. I was hoping one of the willow people would get paint on it and not be able to camouflage itself."
"Gary, what are you doing there?"
"God, I hope the traps will hold..."
"Goddamit, Gary..."

"Good question. Being a phasmid, of the order *phantasmodea* -- a ghost insect -- it disguises itself as plant-matter. In this case the reeds..." He looks around. "Awful lot of reeds around, aren't there?"
"Good to see you again, officer. To what do I owe the pleasure?"
"Good, okay..." He breaks his calm. "*And?*"
"Good. A good quality to have -- both for a police officer *and* an experimental zoologist."
"Ha ha, nothing like the gratitude of a good woman. Now, then, what can I do for you?" He gives you a gruff pat on the shoulder.
"Hate to break it to you, Gary, but rhinos don't just combust in flames."
"Hell no, I had no idea. And I'm still cross with him to be honest. It's not like him. He's got his quirks, but dishonesty -- or disloyalty -- are not one of them."
"Hello hello!" He gets up. "What can I do for you, officer?"
"Hello! Lena and I were just discussing the design of the new trap."
"Hello, officer! I think I almost have it! A new trap design, that is! I know you're sceptical, but I have a good feeling about this."
"Here we go. Nice and easy. No way out, little guys, not out of this jam..."

"Here's a fresh batch of locusts. They should slide right down the funnel. And thank you again. We will definitely mention you, should this lead to a discovery. I'm not talking co-discovery, of course, but..."
"Hmh," a hum and a nod. "My methods do not differ from other scientists, I simply draw upon a wider variety of evidence, and I have more hope that something truly surprising might happen."
"Hmm! Well, first of all it's damn difficult to find -- which is why we've been knee-deep in the reeds laying traps for it."
"Hmph. I appreciate your concern, *officer*, but please leave this to the *experts*. Unless you have an *alternative* hypothesis you'd like to venture..."
"Honestly, I doubt you'd find any of it comprehensible."
"How about rekindling that camp fire so we can dry off?"
"How could she? Who imagines this? She didn't *know* about the phasmid. This is the main thing here, what makes it a confirmed sighting -- she had no previous knowledge of the insect."
"Huh? No. No, of course not. Why?"
"Human remains *have* been found deep in the forest, torn apart, then trampled into the mulch by large hooves. Infer from *that* what you will."
"I *know* it's real," the cryptozoologist says, brusquely enough that even he seems taken aback by it...
"I HEARD THAT, GARY!"
"I chased it with a net -- not very elegant, but you can't be elegant in the field -- and, well, it was faster than me!"
"I couldn't possibly shower thanks on you as enthusiastically as my wife has," he says with a friendly nod. "But I am grateful for your assistance, officer."
"I definitely left that one stocked. Hmm..."
"I didn't expect you to take such an interest in our work here, officer." He looks at you with obvious surprise.
"I doubt that. Once confirmed a hoax, so-called sightings of the rhino stopped." A cough. "Was there anything else, or..."
"I fear this mindless barbarism may have wiped out the elusive creature entirely. Sightings of *towering luminosities* have grown rare recently. While they once used to be constant..."
"I have to resist the thought." He shakes his head vigorously. "Such an extraordinary creature is doubtlessly *highly resilient*. After all, it's generally thought to be capable of parthenogenesis."
"I have yet to *catch* a cryptid, if that's what you're getting at, but I have come close."
"I haven't had a chance to travel to *Koko Nur*, no. And I likely never will. The Samarskilt desert region has been embroiled in a small civil war for the last eight years."
"I just have to do one more round, see if the phasmid has taken the bait... Then we're going." He refastens a bit of netting that has come loose in the wind.
"I know you think we were snacking on funny mushrooms. It's easier to mock someone than to admit that the world might be more interesting than you've imagined."

"I'm Morell, a cryptozoologist. I'm out here looking for a rare insect called the *Insulindian phasmid*. I'd shake your hand, but..." He displays his gloved hands, which are glistening with silt and sewage.
"I'm afraid not, officer. I've been busy digging around in the reeds for days, looking for signs of insect activity -- I'm less interested in mammalian concerns, to be perfectly honest."
"I'm doing this for *science*. And so is she."
"I'm expecting it to be quite giant. One known species of phasmid, called the *megaphasmodea zhouensis*, is about the size of a grown man's forearm. So..." He leaves the conclusion up to you.
"I'm fine, Lena..." He coughs. "And I definitely won't have a heart attack. Rather a cough fit..."
"I'm guessing you heard about it from Lena," he smiles. "The kind green ape is one of her favourites."
"I'm looking for a rare insect, the *Insulindian phasmid*. Field work -- nothing quite like it..."
"I'm not an *adventurer*, I'm a *scientist*. I know how to tread lightly and clean up after myself."
"I've just always liked animals, and puzzles. Searching for cryptids is a bit of both."

"If it weren't for Lena, I might've given up hope years ago. It's no exaggeration to say that she restored my faith in my profession." He looks at her with admiration, forgetting a wide smile on his face.
"If you see Lena, tell her I won't be long," he says, getting up. "I'm so close to being done here..."
"In fact -- it is 0.05%. Ever more magnificent, should our search contribute to making that number 0.075%!"

"In fact, we may be close to capturing a live specimen. Modern genetic methods may prove *crucial* in differentiating the dread variant from the herbivorous one. Anyway..." He gestures for you to continue.
"Indeed. My methods do not differ from other scientists, I simply draw upon a wider variety of evidence, and I have more hope that something truly surprising might happen."

"Indeed." He does not smile, just looks you in the eye. It's a forceful gaze. "If our expedition is successful, every paper in the world will report on it. From Revachol to Doushantou -- it will be a zoological miracle."
"Insane. Yes. Okay. Good." He quickly comes to terms with it. "But you said the water lock is fixed now, so we can go back..."

"It *is* precious. A single dose cost me 50 reál to develop. Not that I expect *you* to understand self-financing one's own research." He looks at the lieutenant with disdain, then puts the spray back in his pocket.
"It makes sense that such a majestic animal with natural weapons -- antlers -- would come to rule the forest. The only strange thing is that it took so long."
"It's a bit crowded in here."
"It's great to see you again, officer!" He grins, bowing awkwardly. "My wife can't wait to thank you. Go on, talk to her."
"It's made of musk and research chemicals. The pheromones *should* attract the insect to you, or at least prevent it from bolting at the sight of you. It's quite potent, will last you about a week."
"It's my hypothesis that it has evolved certain electro-chemical defences that allow it to interfere with animal perception -- impeding pattern recognition, confusing the visual cortex."
"It's not child's play just because I have to traipse through the mud every so often." His eyes narrow.
"It's the first credible sighting in several decades. Admittedly, it's an unusual location for this species, but with all the sewage run-off upstream, it probably doesn't matter much anymore."
"It's truly not that special. What is *cryptozoology* anyway? A derogative. I just like puzzles, like any scientist."
"Just like an ordinary Ardan moose."
"Kids? What would a *child* want with bugs?"
"Locusts." He gestures toward the trap. "Nearly all *known* phasmids are herbivores, of course, but we've hypothesized that the Insulindian phasmid might occasionally prey on other insects."

"Many of them probably are. Statistically speaking, about 20% of all cryptids are verified hoaxes. Uncovering falsehoods deliberately fabricated to fool the public is just as much my calling as finding new species."
"Many times. It always turns into an argument. I don't want to repeat it. The rhino holds a special place in his heart -- let it. Myths are part of my field."
"Me -- I'm not a people person, unless you haven't noticed. And I don't make a good lecturer. My strength lies in field work and *persistence*." He brushes an errant strand of hair from his eye.
"Mijanou liked *extreme* animals, you see. One of the few figures of the academic establishment I respect. Really a shame she disappeared."
"Modern radar telemetry shows great promise -- we *will* confirm this one. By the end of the decade, latest."
"Moose are already being hunted for sport. Can you imagine what would happen if they came to be viewed as predators?"
"Morell, cryptozoologist. I'd shake your hand, but..." He displays his gloved hands, which are glistening with sewage and silt.

"Most *establishment* scientists only care about reputation and remuneration, not *real* research, and certainly not the truth. They're a cowardly lot, and both *the field* and basement archives can be dangerous places."
"Mutation..." the man scoffs. "All of evolution is a mutation."
"My methods are the same as those of other scientists, I simply draw upon a wider variety of evidence, and I have more hope that something truly surprising might happen."
"My wife understands that just as well as anyone." He looks south -- where Lena would be.
"Nature does not concern herself with ethical propositions. As a scientist, my interest is *strictly dispassionate*."
"No -- that is precisely what we're *not*. We are zoological specialists, looking for an extant species of phasmid."

"No offence, officer, but I'm not much of a *pedagogue* -- I don't know what I would've done if Lena hadn't persuaded me to go back to field research. You should ask her, if you want interesting stories."
"No, no, no. The traps need to be monitored on a regular schedule. What would we do if the phasmid were to *starve* while we were sipping tea at the hostel?"
"No, officer. You've got the wrong person. I deal with *living* organisms."
"No-no. No need to apologize, Gary. You've been more than helpful. We'll have to take a rain check on that game of 'Suzerainty' today though -- we're gonna follow this through."

"No. I will not *get* out of anywhere." He lashes immediately. "The dread moose is a widely reported cryptid from Arda. It subsists entirely on flesh, and has even been known to dig up fresh graves in search of sustenance."
"No. Very few cryptids are ever discovered -- and not for a lack of trying. To stay hidden is a cryptid's primary quality. It's even in the *name* cryptid."
"Not *yet*" He holds up an index finger. "That's what makes it a *cryptid*.
"Not all of them." He answers for her. "There is some white colouration reported, along with beige, where the camouflage ends."
"Of course -- be *sarcastic*." He misinterprets your words. "Unless you have an *alternative* hypothesis you'd like to venture, mine stands, okay?"
"Of course it's important to her, she's *seen* it. A verified sighting, on record, one of only four this century and it's hers."
"Of course you haven't." He seems satisfied.
"Of the list of cryptids kept by the Cryptozoological Society of Chemnie, which is four thousand and eighty two items long, about two thousand have been confirmed as hoaxes."
"Oh good. We should really be getting back. Gary could use a hot shower and a warm bed..."
"Oh no, it's alright. I'm just busy." He glances at the cylinder. "What's this about?"
"Oh yes, officer. Very much so. The traps are all in the reeds -- that is where we expect the phasmid to prowl."

"Oh, I *doubt* there's any connection there. Anyway, these pheromones will attract the insect to you, or at least prevent it from bolting at the sight of you. It's quite potent, should last you about a week."
"Oh, decades ago. In the Thirties. I didn't know her personally, of course. A chasm of academic pretension still stood before us, even though she had unusual courage for someone from the other side."
"Oh, everyone knows about that one, thanks to professor Mijanou being the talk of the town for a time..." He coughs in his fist.
"Oh, hello, officer." He covers his mouth, struggling to suppress a coughing fit.
"Oh, you're just talking about *humans*. Well, yes, we are quite dangerous, but we're hardly cryptids." He corrects his hat and says -- as if it's the most sensible thing in the world...
"Okay..." He eyes you sceptically. "I already did my best to inform you. I don't really know what else I could discuss with a layman..."
"One slaughterhouse at the outskirts of the woods in Vaasa reported that its staff kept seeing moose in the distance."
"Pardon me. This is... a big deal for us. You've helped us *twice* now -- and brought great news too. My gratitude, *and* the gratitude of the Société Cryptozoologique de Revachol, is yours."
"Parthe-no-genesis. Meaning the females don't need males to reproduce. Makes it easier for a species to survive in adverse conditions."
"REALLY? You kept complaining how dirty everything is, but we digress..."
"Really, it's too much, officer..." He starts coughing again.
"Really, officer, we can take it from here." The cryptozoologist furrows his heavy brow.
"Remarkable! When?"
"Scientist. Yes. Okay." He quickly comes to terms with it. "But you said the water lock is fixed now, so we can go back..."
"Simple -- attracted by the locusts, the phasmid crawls down the funnel, and, having eaten its fill, can't get back out."
"So it *was* just a child..." He purses his lips, crestfallen.
"Sometimes it's helpful to take a break and return to one's *primary pursuit* with fresh eyes." He nods.
"Suffice to say, it's long been our dream to find proof of the Insulindian phasmid *together*. I can't abandon course now." Another cough, into his fist this time.
"Sure, why not?" He scowls.
"Sure." He quickly comes to terms with this. "But you said the water lock is fixed now, so we can go back..."
"THE HELL, GARY?! YOU IN TROUBLE?"
"Thank you for the vote of no-confidence, Gary. And *officer*, I appreciate your concern, but please leave this to the *experts*. Unless you have an *alternative* hypothesis you'd like to venture..."
"Thank you for your help. Gary and I will start breaking down camp. If you have any more questions, now's the time to ask! We'll be gone once you get to it."
"Thank you for your help. Gary and I will start breaking down camp. If you have any more questions, now's the time to ask!"
"Thank you for your opinion. We have also included plant material in the traps -- to satiate your *scepticism*."
"That it will." The man cracks an unwieldy smile. "That it *absolutely* will. I hope you brought your good boots."
"That's *highly* unlikely, officer. But, in the event you do..." He takes out a small white spray can. "I'll spray you with a pheromone mixture I developed."
"That's impressive, I guess." He does not seem that impressed. "But have you *seen* it with your own eyes?"
"That's not *ideal*, but..." He rubs his chin.
"That's what I thought. You haven't *actually* seen it. And I can't imagine how you could either -- the Samarskilt desert region has been embroiled in a civil war for the last eight years."
"That's what I thought. You haven't *actually* seen it. In fact, I can't imagine how you could either -- the Samarskilt desert region has been embroiled in a civil war for the last eight years."
"The bodies found in the forest are just one piece of physical evidence. There's more -- sightings in Vaasa, reaching back *four centuries*. But, of course, nothing satiates the scepticism of..."
"The bodies found in the forest are just one piece of physical evidence. There's more..."
"The carnivorous moose are a very young species, the result of a genetic mutation that fared well in the process of natural selection."
"The evidence is right there -- we can't just ignore it."
"The moose would just stare at the building, as though they were waiting for something. Its eyes bloodshot and full of *cruelty*."
"The most dangerous cryptid is a carnivorous ruminant, known colloquially as the *dread moose*."
"The recent surge in the moose population. As hidden carnivores, the dread moose are effectively removing competition for both themselves and their evolutionary cousins."
"The search was fabulously unsuccessful -- but the people were very nice. I'm glad they didn't understand what Gary was saying about them..."
"The third is set near the canal, where you crossed. By a concrete slab. A big thicket of reeds going up the slope, and among them..." He gestures to the trap in front of him.
"The what?"
"There are four in total. One is to the south, on this little peninsula -- by the boat houses there." He points south. "It's very near."
"There was a confirmed sighting in Mirova in December."
"There was a credible sighting here recently. A pair of teenagers described a creature that matched the Insulindian phasmid to an *uncanny* degree, *despite* not knowing what it was themselves."
"They'll *work*, I assure you. The predatory hypothesis -- using locusts as bait -- accounts for the failure of previous efforts by other teams, which used plants. We have given this some thought."
"They're not people, really -- some argue that they're not even animals, as they seem to have evolved directly from trees." He says it in a self-explanatory, every day manner.

"They're very, very thin, almost flat, in fact, and can camouflage themselves easily, wrapping themselves around trees and blending in with the tree bark. In that way, they're not too dissimilar from the phasmid we are looking for here."
"To what do I owe the pleasure?"
"Two are categorized as 'confirmed discoveries'. The rest are in differing stages of discovery, refutation, and data collection."
"Typical rookie assumption." He flashes you a sideways smile. "Insects are much more sophisticated creatures than those unversed in zoology give them credit for."
"Understood, lieutenant." The man tips his hat slightly and then looks to you.
"Very little, I'm sorry to say. No one's ever captured a specimen, so all our information is based on first- and third-hand accounts."
"Very, *very* hard."
"WHAT DID YOU DO, GARY?!"
"We cryptozoologists are brutally honest with ourselves, more so even than the public. Most cryptids are hoaxes or they are never found. That does not mean we should stop searching."
"We travelled to South Safre to look for it once. Gary and I got stuck in a rainstorm, though, and had to spend most of our time there in a little village."
"We were on a date, can you imagine? She tells me a story and it's the most detailed report of the Insulindian phasmid I've ever heard. The sounds -- she told me it hissed..."
"We were supposed to go back to Martinaise a couple of days ago, but that damned water lock is broken." He gives a dismissive wave.
"We'll be on our way soon." He gets up. "Thank you again for lending a hand."
"Well..." He doesn't know what to say. "Be that as it may, I'd really appreciate the help!"
"Well..." He lowers his voice. "He's been a little unenthusiastic about the trip. More so than usual. But that's understandable. He just wants to get home and warm up."
"Well..." He points at the cage of mesh and wiring on the ground. "They may not *look* impressive, but Lena designed them quite cleverly, so I'm sure they'll do the trick."
"What did you do, Gary?"
"What the devil is a Cuno? And why would he be making a *city of bugs*?"
"What the devil... Why would kids be making a *city of bugs*?"
"When it's not hunting its prey in this manner, the Okk hangs from tree branches, like a bat, waiting to dive on hapless prey below, on the jungle floor."
"Who's there? Oh, the police. Hello, officer."
"Who's there? Oh, the police. Hello, officers."
"Why?" He spreads his arms in disbelief.
"Wilderness?" He looks around. "You must be joking, officer."
"YES, GARY! WE CAN GO BACK SOON!" He turns to you. "If you see Lena, tell her I won't be long now."
"YES, GARY! WE CAN GO BACK SOON!" He turns to you.
"YES, GARY! WE CAN GO SOON!" He turns to you. "If you see Lena, tell her I won't be long."
"YES, GARY! WE CAN GO SOON!" He turns to you.
"Yes -- the Shautauquan forest pygmy who turned out to be an extinct species of primate; and a cave salamander from Yugo-Graad, who is... honestly quite unremarkable. It's in a zoo somewhere..."
"Yes! The *phantasmodea* picked off the locusts and escaped. This is good news! Though we'll have to reconsider the design of the traps, make them *more* secure..."
"Yes, indeed! Both require a great deal of research, attention to detail, and, above all, *persistence*."
"Yes, the Insulindian phasmid is a *very* clever insect -- that's why it's so damn difficult to catch! But as a scientist, I try my best to remain dispassionate."
"Yes, the most *recent* sighting was by a couple of teenagers along the coast here. That's what brought us to Martinaise specifically."
"Yes, yes, I am." He looks at you with mild surprise, then quickly recovers --
"Yes, you're right. We just need to restock the empty trap. Then we'll need to inspect the traps one more time, and then *maybe*... we can..."
"Yes," he says with some pride.
"Yes-yes -- *and*?"

"Yes. I know it sounds like we were snacking on funny mushrooms -- but I did see motion and colour. Mine is not a *confirmed* sighting of a cryptid, however. Much goes into *verifying* these things, and my account comes short of a few standards."
"Yes. Probably." Another cough. His face grows reddish from it.
"Yes. That's... how we first came to know one another, in fact. But that's *her* story to tell, not mine." He coughs, then continues...
"Yes. The dread moose subsists entirely on flesh. It has even been known to dig up fresh graves in search of sustenance."
"Yes. The females don't need males to reproduce. Makes it easier for a species to survive in adverse conditions."
"Yes. What?"
"Yes?"
"You broke the water lock with a motor carriage? But there was a billboard in the canal..." He looks south. "Not a vehicle. It said 'Samaran Butter.'"
"You can't! That's what makes it so dreadful... and hard to identify."
"You kept complaining about how dirty they were."
"You probably have!"
"You should check at least one of those before returning to *this* one, since I just set it. This one's more of a *technicality*, but still... better safe and stupid than sorry."
"You were a *child*, my dear. Really, it's extraordinary what you were able to describe. Now go on, tell our friend about it. He's proven his interest in the field."
"You're right to." He gives you an approving tip of his hat. "The bodies found in the forest are just one piece of physical evidence. We also have sightings in Vaasa, reaching back *four centuries*."
"You're right, Lena. The RCM is worth their salt -- more so than they say on the radio."
"You're right, dear. We'll get our shot yet, I'm sure of it..."
"You're right, dear." His face relaxes. "It's a fair point. But what other explanation could there be?" He turns to you.
"You're right, you're right..." He breathes carefully, not to start coughing again. "We can come back next season... when it's warmer..."
"Your choice." He puts the spray back in his pocket. "As I said, the chances of you encountering the phasmid are next to zero."
